newsitem.title: PERU: Former guerrilla urges talks in Lima hostage crisis.
newsitem.headline: Former guerrilla urges talks in Lima hostage crisis.

text.p: The Colombian guerrilla leader who captured the Dominican Embassy in Bogota in 1980 for two months says negotiations are the only way out of Peru's 92-day hostage crisis.
"Let's talk! Let's talk! What is needed is a climate of dialogue," Rosemberg Pabon, the former M-19 guerrilla known as "Comandante Uno," recommended at a seminar on Tuesday night.

He said the Peruvian government and the Tupac Amaru rebels holding 72 VIPs inside the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima must both give ground if a peaceful solution is to be found to Latin America's longest hostage ordeal.
"You have to back down," said Pabon, who now works as an academic and adviser to local governments in Colombia.

Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas blasted through a wall and stormed a diplomatic reception, seizing hundreds of guests. They are demanding the release of more than 400 jailed rebels in exchange for the hostages' lives.

The siege is similar to Pabon's M-19 assault on the embassy in Bogota, where his band of 15 rebels held 57 diplomats and other hostages for 61 days before taking $2 million and a plane to asylum in Cuba.
Seventeen years later, Pabon said he disagreed with the taking of hostages for political ends.
Geraldo do Nascimento e Silva, the former Brazilian ambassador to Colombia and one of Pabon's hostages, shook hands with his former captor over breakfast at the seminar.

He said the greatest danger for hostages was from outside. "We did not feel endangered by the M-19 but from the outside. We felt we had to do everything possible to avoid a military solution," the former diplomat said.
Fears of a violent end to the Peruvian crisis have risen with the slow progress of talks between the two sides.
